_status:
THIS FILE IS NOW THE CATALOG, not a highlight reel. Rebuilt 2026-09-15 from Connor's dish sheet: 73 rows covering the six San Diego rooms, against the 14 it carried before.

WHAT THE OLD NOTE SAID AND WHY IT IS GONE. It read "INCOMPLETE AND NOT LAUNCH-READY ... this is NOT the per-location menu" and pointed at Open Decision #12, which the Toast pull closed on 2026-08-04. The sheet closes the rest: per-room availability for every row, from the operator.

WHY IT HAD TO GROW. The sheet shows there is no brand-wide menu worth the name. Eight dishes are served at all six rooms and eight more at five, all missing only Plaza Bonita. Mercury carries 47 rows against Crown Point's 21 and is a substantially different restaurant. A 14-row file could not describe that, so /menu/ was describing a menu nobody serves.

PRICES ARE STILL ABSENT AND STAY ABSENT. Every new row carries price: null. See _priceStatus.
_availabilityStatus: SEEDED 2026-08-04 from all seven live Toast catalogs. Open Decision #12 closes. Every row's `locations` is derived by exact name match against src/_data/toastMenus/*.json through an explicit alias table, because three separate substring matchers on this project produced wrong answers. TWO ALIASES ARE NAME CONFLICTS, not typos, and are flagged in _nameConflicts below.
_descriptionStatus:
TWO KINDS OF DESCRIPTION IN THIS FILE, and they are not equally settled.

1. DRAFT, PENDING CLIENT APPROVAL. The rows carried over from the design concept (tonkotsu, red, black, white, spicy sesame, vegan) are ingredient lists from that artifact with unconfirmed claims removed: the concept's 'simmered twelve hours' has no source in CLIENT_FACTS.md and is not repeated here, and no description asserts anything about flour, hydration, water, alkalinity, aging or noodle cadence. Amanda must sign these off before launch.

2. THE CLIENT'S OWN WORDS, from their 2026-07 printed menus in public/menus/. Curry Ramen (added 2026-09-10) and, from 2026-09-14, Pork Gyoza, Karaage, Garlic Edamame, Matcha Panna Cotta, Chicken Ramen and Carnitas Ramen. Each carries a _descriptionSource quoting the printed line it came from and naming every room whose menu prints it. These still want a sign-off, but they are transcription rather than drafting, which is a different thing to be asked to approve.

NOTHING IN THIS FILE IS GENERATED, AND NOTHING MAY BE. CLAUDE.md: menu items, descriptions and prices are never generated or modified without explicit client approval. If a dish has no description on the printed menus, it gets a null and waits. Miso Ramen is the one such row: see its _descriptionGap.
_priceStatus:
NOT FOR DISPLAY. RESOLVED 2026-09-10 at client review: /menu/ prints no prices at all, and the per-location printable menus in public/menus/ are the only place a price appears on this site.

THE FIELD STAYS AND MUST NOT BE RENDERED. It is a record of what the brand prices were, and deleting it would lose that record, but every value in it is stale and none may reach a page. History, for whoever reads this next: as of 2026-08-04 nine of the thirteen were below live Convoy, every ramen by fifty cents except Miso Ramen, which was fifty cents OVER; the four appetiser and dessert prices matched Convoy exactly. Prices also vary by room, with Plaza Bonita below the other San Diego rooms and Maui above them, so a single brand price could never have been right for all seven. The 2026-07 printed menus confirmed both of those findings.

No `offers` is emitted in schema and none should be. Verified 2026-09-10: no price string reaches any built page, and the schema graph contains no offers and no price.
_carnitasNote:
PERMANENT AND PHOTOGRAPHED, CONFIRMED BY THE CLIENT AT REVIEW 2026-09-10. This supersedes the 2026-08-04 position, which was that the dish ships as a plain line with feature: no and 'no photo, no card, no callout, no hero'. That position came from brand positioning wanting the dish phased out quietly. The client has now said it stays.

WHAT CHANGED AND WHAT DID NOT. It has a photograph on /menu/ now. The 'feature' flag stays FALSE on purpose: setting it true would also put the dish in the location-page bentos and the per-room menu lists, and 'permanent and gets a photo' is not the same instruction as 'promote it everywhere'. If the client wants that too, set feature to true and the rest follows on its own with no template change.

Availability is confirmed active at all seven locations (live Toast menus, 2026-08-04) and again by all six 2026-07 printed menus in public/menus/. scripts/build-photo-manifest.js no longer excludes Carnitas photographs: five are now in the manifest and one is placed. The other five do-not-feature dishes are unchanged and still have no photograph anywhere.

This is what finally closes SITE_ARCHITECTURE.md Open Decision #21: DESIGN_SYSTEM.md and voice-tone.md carried blanket bans that contradicted the shipped page, and both are corrected as of 2026-09-10.

items._pulled:
PULLED 2026-09-15. Served at zero locations.

TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES AGREE and they resolve what was an open question. Connor's 2026-09-15 dish sheet marks this row at zero of six rooms, and all six 2026-07 printed menus in public/menus/ omit the dish entirely. Before today this row claimed all six on the strength of the Toast pull alone.

THE TOAST CATALOGS STILL DISAGREE and that is recorded, not erased. The live catalogs pulled 2026-08-04 list "Naruto Miso Ramen" at all six San Diego rooms. So: two sources say the dish is not served, one says it is, and the one that says it is calls it by a different name. See _nameConflicts.

WHAT TO ASK: is Naruto Miso Ramen still served, and if so why is it on neither the printed menus nor the dish sheet? A Toast catalog can carry a retired item; a printed menu and a hand-kept sheet agreeing that it is gone is the stronger reading, which is why the row is at zero rather than deleted. The row survives with its description and its history so restoring it is one edit.

The description arrived in the same pass, from the sheet, and is kept: if the dish comes back we will not have to source it again.

items._source:
ADDED 2026-09-10 on Steve's instruction, with the photograph he supplied. DESCRIPTION IS THE CLIENT'S OWN, lifted from the 2026-07 Convoy printed menu in public/menus/ and put into this file's house style, which is the same transform every other row here has had: 'original spicy pork bone broth mixed with special spiced curry, noodles, seasoned ground pork, 1/2 ramen egg, broccoli, corn, diced onions, dried chili pepper, and sesame seeds'. Nothing was written. Every element in it is visible in the photograph.

PRICE IS NULL AND STAYS NULL. /menu/ prints no prices as of 2026-09-10, and the printed menu's figure is Convoy's, not a brand price.

CONVOY ONLY, and this is the only row in this file with a single-location availability. Three independent sources agree: the seven live Toast catalogs pulled 2026-08-04 carry Curry Ramen at Convoy and nowhere else, the six 2026-07 printed menus show it on Convoy's only, and CLIENT_FACTS.md's College Heights correction says in as many words that the only ramen absent there is Curry Ramen. That is why it carries an availabilityNote: a reader on /menu/ would otherwise reasonably expect it at their room.

NO `emphasis`. The name renderer on /menu/ strips the emphasis word AND the word Ramen from the heading, then italicises the emphasis. That is right for Traditional Tonkotsu, which becomes TRADITIONAL TONKOTSU. With emphasis 'Curry' this row rendered as a bare CURRY sitting next to CHICKEN RAMEN and CARNITAS RAMEN, which read as a different kind of thing. Left null so the full name prints.

It is layout, not content. `tier` is a positioning label sourced from CLIENT_FACTS.md: tonkotsu is 'the foundation dish' and Red/Black/White are 'the signature trio'. Do not invent new tier labels.
_nameConflicts: menu.json's names do NOT match what Toast calls two of these dishes. Recorded rather than changed, because renaming a menu item is a client decision. (1) `Tajima White` is called `Tajima Ramen` on all six San Diego catalogs and `Tajima WHITE Ramen` on Maui. So the San Diego menu has no item literally called Tajima White, and the site currently prints one. (2) `Miso Ramen` is called `Naruto Miso Ramen` everywhere it appears, and the description names a Naruto fishcake that menu.json does not mention.
_imageStatus: REPOINTED 2026-08-05 from cdn.circulationstudio.com/tajima-temp/*.jpeg to the committed local WebP in public/images/photo/. Same photographs, matched by exact basename, verified present in photos.json. Reasons: it drops a third-party origin off the image path on /menu/, /, /tajima-convoy/ and /menu/vegan-ramen/, it serves WebP instead of JPEG, and the temp CDN is temporary by name. imageWidth and imageHeight are the manifest real pixel dimensions and exist so templates can stop hardcoding 800x800, which was wrong for every one of these (they are 3:2, not square). ALT TEXT IS UNCHANGED: it was already hand-written here and is better than the photos.json draft placeholders. Only 6 of 13 items carry an image; the other 7 are deliberately imageless rather than mapped on a guess.
_imageGapNote: Five images added 2026-08-05 from photos already classified as mapped in photos.json, each checked by eye before placing rather than trusted from its dish token. TWO ITEMS ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT WITHOUT ONE. (1) carnitas: Open Decision #4 resolved it as listed plainly on /menu/ and nowhere else, explicitly no photo, no card, no callout. (2) miso: the manifest maps three files to dish 'miso' and ALL THREE ARE MISO SOUP, a small lacquer bowl of soup with scallion and wakame, not Naruto Miso Ramen. The token matched the word, not the dish. Do not place them. The same trap sits on the 'chicken' token, which groups chicken fried rice, chicken katsu bun and chicken teriyaki alongside the real Chicken Ramen: only the two files named chicken-ramen are the bowl. Treat photos.json dish tokens as candidates to inspect, never as a mapping to apply.
_printedMenus:
WHAT THE 2026-07 PRINTED MENUS CORROBORATE, recorded 2026-09-09 without transcribing prices. Files in public/menus/, provenance in src/_data/locationMenus.json.

The per-location availability in this file, derived from the live Toast catalogs on 2026-08-04, holds up against the client's own print: Curry Ramen appears only on Convoy, matching CLIENT_FACTS.md's College Heights correction; Plaza Bonita offers Tajima Red or White and not Black, matching the `locations` arrays here; East Village carries a sushi hand roll with a salmon or spicy tuna choice, matching the 2026-08-04 correction to CLIENT_FACTS.md; Mercury is the only room with a full sushi section. Two separate sources, derived independently, agree.

ITEMS ON THE PRINTED MENUS THAT ARE NOT IN THIS FILE, and this file is not wrong for lacking them: Plaza Bonita has a Mini Ramen, an onigiri range, spam musubi and numbered combo sets; Mercury has a kids section, a monthly-specials izakaya section and a named roll list. This file is the brand menu that /menu/ renders, not a per-room catalog, and expanding it into one is a content decision nobody has taken.
_availabilityNoteRule: `availabilityNote` is visible copy and MUST agree with `locations` on the same row. It exists because /menu/ speaks for seven rooms and one row is not available at all of them. Curry Ramen is the only row that carries one today. If `locations` changes, change the note in the same edit or delete it: a stale availability note is worse than none, because it sends someone to a room for a bowl that is not there.
_zeroLocationRows:
SEVEN ROWS ARE SERVED AT ZERO LOCATIONS in Connor's 2026-09-15 sheet: Brussels Sprouts Tempura, Chicken Katsu Bowl, Glazed Popcorn Shrimp, Karaage Bowl, Miso Ramen, Steam Rice, Vegetable Gyoza.

ONLY MISO RAMEN IS RESOLVED. It is at zero in the sheet AND absent from all six printed menus, which is two independent sources. See its _pulled note.

THE OTHER SIX ARE NOT A DECISION, THEY ARE A QUESTION, and the question is narrower than it looks. VEGETABLE GYOZA HAS A REAL, EYE-VERIFIED PHOTOGRAPH in the manifest (tajima-ramen-vegetable-gyoza-kihei.webp: five dumplings in pale green wrappers, browned on one side, with a cup of dipping sauce, visibly a different dish from Pork Gyoza). Nobody photographs a dish they have discontinued. So at least one of these six zeroes is a data gap rather than a deletion, which changes the question from "should we pull these six" to "which of these six is Connor missing".

ASK CONNOR, per row: discontinued, or not yet filled in? Until then they are listed here with empty `locations`, which means they render nowhere and claim nothing. That is the safe state in both directions: no room advertises a dish it does not serve, and no dish is deleted on a maybe.
_sheetSource:
src: _reference/Tajima_Menu_260915_photos-updated.xlsx, Connor, 2026-09-15. 74 dish rows, one sheet.

COLUMN LETTERS, stated here because the first brief had them off by one and the next pass should not repeat it:
  A  Dish Name
  B  Dish Type
  C  Dish Description
  D  Photo of Dish (Link)   <- the Bunny URL. NOT column E.
  E  # of Locations         <- a count, derived; it agrees with F to K on
                               every row, checked.
  F  College Heights
  G  Convoy
  H  Crown Point
  I  East Village
  J  Mercury
  K  Plaza Bonita

THERE IS NO MAUI COLUMN. The sheet speaks for the six San Diego rooms only, so Maui's availability is untouched by it and still comes from the Toast pull of 2026-08-04.

ROWS 61 TO 75 ARE APPENDED OUT OF TYPE ORDER, which looks like a second data-entry pass. It matters: reading the sheet naively makes it look as though 39 dishes are served at exactly one room, because that tail splits some dishes the earlier rows already cover. _listedVsFeaturable:
TWO FIELDS, SPLIT OUT OF ONE ON 2026-09-15, and the split is load-bearing.

  listed      Does this dish appear on the menu of a room that serves it?
              TRUE ON EVERY ROW. `locations` says which rooms; this says that
              being served and being printed are the same thing. A room's page
              is that room's menu now, so anything it serves is on it.

  featurable  May this dish take a hero, a card, a callout or a photo slot?
              This is the only field the CLIENT_FACTS.md do-not-feature list
              governs.

WHY IT HAD TO SPLIT. There was one field, `feature`, and it meant both. That
was harmless while a location page showed a curated bento of highlights:
`feature: false` meant "not in the highlight reel". It stopped being harmless
the moment the location page became the room's full menu, because then the
same false meant "absent from the menu of a room that serves it". Six dishes
were affected and the site would have shipped a menu that disagrees with the
menu on the table, which is the exact failure CLIENT_FACTS.md warns about
under Carnitas Ramen.

WHAT IT FIXES FOR CARNITAS. Open Decision #4 says listed plainly, and the
2026-09-10 client review added that it is permanent and has a photograph. Both
are now expressible: listed true, featurable false. It appears in the menu
body of every room that serves it, with its 92px photograph, and it can never
reach a hero, a card, a callout, or the homepage trio. Before the split those
two facts could not both be true.

THE OTHER FIVE do-not-feature dishes (Tajima Fries, Curry Fries, Cream Cheese
Wontons, Crispy Rice Spicy Tuna, Jalapeño Bomb) are the same shape: real
dishes real customers order, listed, never promoted. CLIENT_FACTS.md: "They
are not hidden, they are not the brand voice."

MISO RAMEN is featurable false for a different reason, recorded on its own
row: it was never in the lead-with set. It is also at zero locations, so it
renders nowhere regardless.

EVERY READ OF THE OLD FIELD WAS AUDITED AND REPOINTED. There were five, and
each one had to be decided rather than renamed: eleventy.config.js dishesFor
and schema.js buildMenu ask the LISTED question, menu.njk, the homepage trio
on the frozen concepts route, and build-photo-manifest.js proposedUse ask the
FEATURABLE one. Nothing reads `feature` any more; grep it to be sure.
_trioAvailabilityGap:
THE HOMEPAGE TRIO AND THE AVAILABILITY DATA NO LONGER QUITE AGREE, and this is a client question rather than a bug to fix in the template.

The homepage shows three bowls as the house set: Tajima Red, Tajima Black and Tajima White. Red and White are served at all six San Diego rooms. BLACK IS SERVED AT FIVE, missing only Plaza Bonita, per Connor's 2026-09-15 sheet and per the 2026-07 printed menus, which agree.

So the site presents a trio as the signature of the house while one third of it is unavailable at one of the six rooms. That was invisible while /menu/ listed every dish with no per-room availability on the page. It became visible on 2026-09-15: /menu/ now opens on the eight dishes served at all six rooms, and Black is not among them, so the homepage tile for Black lands beside its two siblings rather than on itself.

IT IS NOT WORTH A PER-DISH PAGE and the tile is not worth breaking up. The real question is the other way round: SHOULD PLAZA BONITA CARRY TAJIMA BLACK? It is a quick-serve room with a focused menu, so the omission may be deliberate. But if the trio is the house signature, a room that serves two thirds of it is a gap in the offer, not just in the data.

ASK: is Tajima Black absent from Plaza Bonita on purpose? If it is, the homepage trio is making a claim about the house that one room does not honor, and the honest options are to add the bowl or to stop calling three bowls the house set. Either is a client call. Nothing on the site currently says the trio is available everywhere, so nothing is wrong today; it is thin ice.
